newsitem.title: JAPAN: Israeli foreign minister defends housing project.
newsitem.headline: Israeli foreign minister defends housing project.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy on Friday defended his country's decision to build houses for Jewish settlers in Arab East Jerusalem, saying the project will benefit both Jewish and Arab communities.
"I am filled with pride that the Israeli cabinet decided to build 3,500 housing units for the Arab population," Levy told a news conference in Tokyo.
"I am hopeful that the two populations living together will enhance the possibility of coexistence," Levy said. He arrived in Tokyo on Wednesday for a five-day visit.
On Wednesday, Israel's ministerial committee on Jerusalem approved the building of 6,500 homes for Jews and more than 3,000 houses for Arabs in East Jerusalem.
Israel's decision sparked international criticism, joined by the United States and Japan, and triggered Palestinian warnings that the plan could unleash bloodshed.
Levy said a majority of land to be used for the new houses was privately owned by Jews.
He said Arabs and the international community should not see a crisis in every small turn because this will endanger the entire Middle East peace process.
"I don't believe this is a make-or-break-issue," Levy said.

Levy met Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto and Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda on Thursday for talks on bilateral ties and the Middle East peace process. Both Hashimoto and Ikeda voiced concern at the East Jerusalem housing project.
Earlier in the day, Levy called on Japanese businesses to boost investment in high-tech, agriculture and desalination projects.
